overall_assessment: Changes required. The operation-bound adapters, shared outbound orchestration, scoped resolution and single acceptance owner substantially follow the frozen architecture. A D04 response-classification defect and an unreliable D10 browser scenario remain. Pending final-all, PCV and post-cutover operator evidence are not treated as completed gates.
recommended_path: Correct the classifier and browser scenario within the approved D04/D10 boundaries, then review the updated candidate and obtain the required validation evidence. No architectural redesign is indicated.

findings.title: Meta refusal classification ignores contradictory IDs after the first message
findings.rationale: api-app/src/integrations/meta/meta.client.ts:219-234 extracts an ID only from messages[0] and uses its absence to establish REJECTED. HTTP 400 with a valid non-transient Graph error code 100 and messages:[{}, {id:'external-ack'}] therefore becomes REJECTED despite containing a contradictory external ID. A malformed first ID, such as messages:[{id:42}], can also reach REJECTED. Frozen D04 requires malformed or contradictory responses to remain UNKNOWN; a definitive refusal here could encourage an unsafe repeat send.
findings.suggested_action: Validate the complete relevant response shape before classification and detect contradictory acceptance markers throughout the messages array. Return UNKNOWN/TRANSPORT_UNCONFIRMED for malformed or contradictory payloads. Add direct HTTP-client regression cases for a non-first external ID and a malformed message ID, retaining the one-request invariant.

findings.title: The delayed-response browser scenario loses its return-navigation target
findings.rationale: web-app/e2e/channel-transport.spec.ts:59-81 first completes an accepted human send, then attempts A→B→A using the Cliente Timeline sidebar button. OutboundService.finalizeOutbound at api-app/src/domain/inbox/outbound.service.ts:233-238 moves A to IN_SERVICE, while Inbox starts on QUEUED and refreshes that filtered list after success. Once refreshed, A is absent from the sidebar, so the return click cannot reliably execute. The line 79 getByText assertion also does not establish that B finished opening: it can match the sidebar alone or become ambiguous with the thread heading. This leaves the required D10 stale-response scenario unreliable.
findings.suggested_action: Arrange navigation so both conversations remain reachable through the appropriate status tabs. Wait for a unique active-thread selector to confirm B and then A have opened before releasing the held response. Assert that the stale completion preserves a newly entered draft and does not introduce an error, then rerun the complete browser/all gate.
